name: TeamPCP
origin: Unknown (low confidence; possible LAPSUS$ connection unconfirmed)
summary: TeamPCP is a financially motivated supply chain threat actor that first surfaced in late 2025 and rapidly evolved from ransomware and cryptomining into a focused software supply chain compromise model. The group is best known for the March 2026 cascading supply chain campaign compromising Trivy, Checkmarx KICS, LiteLLM, and the Telnyx Python SDK via retained credentials, and for authoring the Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm variant released in May 2026. On May 12, 2026 TeamPCP publicly released the Shai-Hulud worm source code, effectively commoditizing the attack technique.

ttps.technique_name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
ttps.notes: Primary vector — npm package poisoning via compromised maintainer credentials
Retained credentials from prior Trivy compromise seeded the March 2026 cascade
Malicious code injected into legitimate package releases
Python SDK poisoning; .pth file auto-execution for persistence
Payload delivery evolved from Base64 to WAV steganography within 8-day campaign window
CI/CD secrets, GitHub tokens, AWS/GCP/Azure keys harvested from pipeline environments
Stolen credentials committed to attacker-controlled GitHub repositories; also committed to victim's own GitHub account
GitHub self-install worker deployed for persistent remote code execution

detection_opportunities: Monitor for unexpected npm package publish events from maintainer accounts
Alert on new GitHub repository creation with name 'Shai-Hulud' under any account
Detect CI/CD secrets access outside normal pipeline execution windows
Monitor for .pth file creation in Python environments
Alert on GitHub Actions workflow modifications touching cache or OIDC endpoints
Detect anomalous cloud API calls (AWS/GCP/Azure) originating from CI infrastructure
Monitor preinstall hook execution in npm dependency trees
